summary.text: 点, the simplified form of 點, is used for a small mark or spot and for a point. Its traditional form combines 黑, ‘black,’ with 占 as a sound element; the present 灬 in 点 belongs to the simplified graphic form, not to that traditional analysis.

formation.text: The traditional character 點 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 黑 contributes the meaning ‘black’ and 占 supplies a phonetic cue. The earliest meaning reported in this analysis is ‘small black mark.’ This construction belongs to 點; the modern lower 灬 of 点 should not be read as evidence that fire was the original semantic component.

components.text: In 點, 黑 is the semantic element: it contributes the black-mark category to the reported original sense, ‘small black mark.’ The form listing records a small-seal witness; it supplies no separate earlier form for this component within 點.
In 點, 占 is identified as the phonetic element. Its own oracle-bone forms are analyzed independently as 卜 plus 口; that history explains 占, not an early form of 點.

sound_limitation.text: The phonetic analysis is reported, but the inspected Middle Chinese categories for 點 and 占 differ, and no independently verified same-system Old Chinese comparison for the relevant readings was obtained. The exact early sound correspondence therefore remains unresolved.

sound.text: The phonetic analysis compares traditional 點 with 占. The dossier gives 點 Middle Chinese 多忝切 (rising tone, Division IV) and 占 多 readings 職廉切 (level tone) and 章豔切 (departing tone); the Middle Chinese categories differ, so this evidence does not quantify the earlier match. Modern Mandarin diǎn contrasts with zhān/zhàn.
sound.component_reading: zhān / zhàn (Mandarin); Middle Chinese 職廉切 / 章豔切
sound.system: Middle Chinese categories and modern Mandarin

components.text: 点 corresponds to traditional 點. Its current lower 灬 is part of the simplified graphic form; the available evidence does not establish a complete graphic path or support treating 灬 as the original semantic element. The relation is between the two character forms, not a component substitution claim.

history.text: The consulted form inventory records a small-seal example of 點 and no oracle-bone or bronze examples. This describes that inventory, not proof that no earlier witness exists. No securely dated earliest inscriptional witness is established here.
點 and 点 are linked as traditional and simplified forms. The evidence establishes their present correspondence, but not the full graphic route or a precise date for the simplified form.

uncertainties.text: The phonetic role of 占 is explicitly reported, but the available comparison does not settle the exact early sound relationship: the supplied Middle Chinese categories differ, and the inspected material lacks an independently verified same-system Old Chinese comparison for both relevant readings.
The seal-script listing does not fix the earliest inscriptional form, and the cited lexical examples do not establish a complete chronology for either the earliest use or later sense changes.

senses.text: The traditional character’s reported original sense is ‘small black mark’; the available evidence does not securely date its earliest lexical attestation.

senses.period: Jin-period example cited; exact earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: A Jin-period text is cited for a spot on otherwise unblemished white jade. Other cited uses include writing over a character, ornamenting, textual punctuation, a liquid drop, and checking or counting. These attestations do not by themselves establish a chronological chain linking the senses.
The character is used for a point; the supplied evidence also lists degree and decimal point among present definitions. It does not establish how each use developed from the older mark sense.

limitations.text: The cited uses support distinct historical meanings, but the evidence does not establish every transition among spots, textual marking, ornamenting, drops, checking, counting, time units, and modern point or degree senses. No semantic chain is asserted.
The earliest lexical attestation is not conclusively fixed by the cited material; the reported small-black-mark sense is not a securely dated first occurrence.

overview.text: 点 means a small mark or spot and can mean a point. It is the simplified form of 點, whose traditional analysis joins 黑, ‘black,’ with 占 as a sound element.

components.text: In traditional 點, 黑 contributes the ‘black’ part of the reported small-black-mark meaning.
占 is identified as the sound element in 點; its own older graphic history does not establish an early form of 點.
The lower 灬 is visible in simplified 点, but the evidence does not identify it as the original meaning element.

takeaway.text: The current 灬 shape should not be taken to mean that fire was the original component in 點.

relationships.text: 黑 contributes the black-mark meaning in the traditional character 點, which is linked to simplified 点.
占 is explicitly identified as the phonetic element in traditional 點; the exact early sound correspondence is unresolved.
The evidence links 点 as the simplified form of traditional 點; it does not specify the complete graphic path or date.
